description: For current-law 2026 individual cases, the refundable-credit aggregate includes the refundable credits modeled in Subpart C and payroll-tax refundable credits, and final federal income tax is income tax before refundable credits reduced by that aggregate.

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: 26 USC 6401(b)(1) defines the aggregate generically as 'the amount allowable as credits under subpart C of part IV of subchapter A of chapter 1', but the pre-fix module hard-coded a modelling list (eitc + refundable_american_opportunity_credit + refundable_ctc + recovery_rebate_credit + refundable_payroll_tax_credit) that is neither traceable to the provision nor confined to subpart C, and it omitted 6401(b)(2)'s rule that a section 33 credit counts only when a 6013(g)/(h) election is in effect (except when allowed by reason of section 1446).
triage.triage_notes: The quote is a verbatim fragment of the deleted module summary; the file wraps it across three lines, which I joined without changing any words. This module also went from encoding only a slice of 6401(b) to encoding 6401(a) (`limitation_period_overpayment_part`), the 6401(b)(1) overpayment output (`refundable_credit_excess_overpayment`) and 6401(c) (`tax_payment_can_be_overpayment_despite_no_tax_liability`) — so unrepresented_clause is an equally defensible kind here; I chose untraceable_branch because the hard-coded credit list is the change that most clearly had no basis in the cited text. `income_tax` also moved from `income_tax_before_refundable_credits - income_tax_refundable_credits` to the statutory phrase 'tax imposed by subtitle A (reduced by the credits allowable under subparts A, B, D, and G)'. The regenerated module now depends on several broad undefined inputs (e.g. `credits_allowable_under_subpart_c_excluding_section_33_for_overpayment`), which is faithful to the text but pushes the work to the composer. Effective dates unchanged at 2026-01-01. Provision not separately resolved; the module's added summary is verbatim corpus text.
triage.verifier_justification: The refutation attempt fails on the source text: the pinned release of 26 USC 6401(b)(1) defines the aggregate generically as "the amount allowable as credits under subpart C of part IV of subchapter A of chapter 1", with no enumeration, while the pre-fix `income_tax_refundable_credits` formula summed a closed modelling list that both overshoots subpart C (`refundable_payroll_tax_credit`, a non-statutory modelling variable the pre-fix summary itself calls "payroll-tax refundable credits") and omits the largest subpart C items (section 31 withheld tax, 35, 36B). The fix does not add a missing carve-out to that list; it deletes the enumeration outright and re-grounds the rule on the statutory subpart C term plus a separately encoded 6401(b)(2) section 33 rule, which is exactly the untraceable_branch operation (a value with no basis in the cited source, removed/re-grounded). The competing kind, unrepresented_clause, describes only the secondary additions (the 6013(g)/(h) election condition and the new 6401(a), (b)(1)-excess and (c) rules), and at the anchored rule path rules[income_tax_refundable_credits].versions[0].formula the decisive change is the removal of the ungrounded list, so the first reader's kind stands.
triage.verifier_notes:
Evidence read: diff 008.diff (whole file, pre 36 lines to post 170), the parent-commit file at 2175d5239a, and the provision via resolve_provision (corpus release us-rulespec-2026-07-13, provision sha 96c1577d...), which confirms (b)(1)'s generic subpart C reference and (b)(2)'s "only if an election under subsection (g) or (h) of section 6013 is in effect" condition with the section 1446 carve-out.

Three caveats for the reviewer:
1. Mixed-kind fix. Besides the re-grounding, the commit adds four rules that are new coverage the pre-fix module never claimed (limitation_period_overpayment_part for 6401(a), refundable_credit_excess_overpayment for the (b)(1) overpayment rule, section_33_credit_treated_as_refundable_credit for (b)(2), tax_payment_can_be_overpayment_despite_no_tax_liability for (c)). Per the task's own guidance those additions alone would not carry a fidelity verdict; the verdict rests solely on the changed formula in the pre-existing income_tax_refundable_credits rule.
2. `income_tax` was also re-grounded: `income_tax_before_refundable_credits` became `tax_imposed_by_subtitle_a_reduced_by_subparts_a_b_d_and_g_credits`. That is closer to a naming/traceability change than a meaning change (the two are roughly the same quantity), so it is weak supporting evidence, not decisive.
3. Executability caveat, and the strongest remaining argument for "unclear": the post-fix formulas reference placeholder variables that the module does not declare or define (`credits_allowable_under_subpart_c_excluding_section_33_for_overpayment`, `tax_imposed_by_subtitle_a_reduced_by_subparts_a_b_d_and_g_credits`, `section_6013_g_or_h_election_in_effect_for_taxable_year`, `amount_of_internal_revenue_tax_payment_assessed_or_collected_after_limitation_period`). The fix trades a runnable modelling implementation for a statutory paraphrase, so if the corpus wants defects whose fix is verifiable by execution rather than by traceability, this case is weaker than the confidence suggests. It is still a genuine meaning disagreement with the source, which is why I did not drop to unclear.

Not applicable: every version keeps effective_from '2026-01-01' pre and post (not wrong_period_or_effective_date); entity stays TaxUnit on the anchored rule (the new 6401(a) rule uses entity Payment, but that rule is new, not a scope correction); no numeric values changed (not amount_mismatch); the only comparison added is max(0, ...) in a newly created rule (not boundary_direction).
